mode.dehydrate.label: Rewrite & polish
mode.dehydrate.description: Rewrites it to read noticeably better — strips the filler, fixes the grammar, and polishes the prose.
mode.interactive.label: Interactive reading
mode.interactive.description: You steer the story — pick the branches and pivotal moments yourself. Just watch your step: the plot doesn't pull its punches.

novel.internet.source.label: Source
novel.internet.source.placeholder: Paste a link, or drop a hint on where to find it.
novel.internet.source.tooltip: Tell me where to read it — a link, a search hint, anything that points the way. It has to be live text on a web page I can open and read, not text baked into an image or a PDF/TXT I'd have to download.
novel.internet.source.hint: Live web text only — no image-locked text, no PDFs or TXT downloads.
options.dehydrate.basic.grammarFix.label: Typos, grammar & punctuation neat-freak
options.dehydrate.basic.grammarFix.toolt: Zero tolerance for typos, mangled grammar, or rogue punctuation — half-matched quotes, orphaned brackets, the works. Reads like it never met a copyeditor? Not anymore.
options.dehydrate.basic.webSlangFilter.l: Filter cringe clichés & undo the censoring
options.dehydrate.basic.webSlangFilter.t: Burned out on 'let out a breath they didn't know they were holding', 'a shiver ran down their spine', and 'could cut the tension with a knife'? Plus all that asterisk-mangled censoring? We're cleaning house — fresh prose in, tired tropes and broken words out.
options.dehydrate.basic.preachRemoval.to: You're here for the story, not the sermon or the lore bible — even when it's disguised as inner monologue. Skip the power-level analysis; let's get to the action.
options.section.cleanup.title: Cleanup
options.section.rewrite.title: Rewrite intensity
options.section.rewrite.hint: Each aspect only applies above Off. Off = skip it; Light / Medium / Heavy = how hard it pushes.
options.section.language.title: Language & translation
options.section.language.tooltip: Optional language transforms — independent, so turn on only what you want; the reader reconciles the rest.
options.section.custom.title: Custom instructions
options.dehydrate.depth.dialoguePacing.t: Tightens the back-and-forth of dialogue so it snaps instead of dragging. Higher = more aggressive trimming and repatterning of speech beats.
options.dehydrate.depth.dialoguePacing.e: e.g. turning a flat 'He said. She said. He said again.' into a punchy exchange.
options.dehydrate.depth.dehydrate.label: Dehydrate & accelerate
options.dehydrate.depth.dehydrate.toolti: Strips filler — redundant beats, padded descriptions, wheel-spinning — so the story actually moves. Higher = more aggressive cutting.
options.dehydrate.depth.dehydrate.exampl: e.g. collapsing three paragraphs of walking-down-the-hall into one line that gets there.
options.dehydrate.depth.sceneEnhance.too: Strengthens place and mood — sensory texture, atmosphere, staging. Higher = richer, more immersive scene-building.
options.dehydrate.depth.sceneEnhance.exa: e.g. turning 'It was a dark room' into something you can actually feel.
options.dehydrate.depth.combatEnhance.to: Punches up fights and set-pieces — impact, pacing, the 'hell yes' beat. Higher = more cinematic and kinetic.
options.dehydrate.depth.combatEnhance.ex: e.g. making a blow-by-blow clash feel weighty instead of clinical.
options.dehydrate.depth.emotionEnhance.t: Deepens feeling and tension — what characters show, hide, and feel. Higher = more intense emotional texture.
options.dehydrate.depth.emotionEnhance.e: e.g. turning 'She was sad' into a proper gut-punch.
Polishes the prose itself — rhythm, word choice, sentence flow. Higher = more stylistic refinement.
e.g. lifting competent sentences into ones that sing.
options.interactive.frequency.label: Interaction frequency
options.source.nonNovel.label: Not chaptered fiction
options.source.nonNovel.tooltip: Turn this on when your source is one continuous block of text that isn't chaptered fiction — a long Reddit post, a blog article, an email thread, a forum thread, and so on. By default the reader assumes chaptered fiction and pulls each chapter from its own page (or splits a file by its chapter markers). With this on, it treats the whole source as a single storyline and writes the chapters itself, breaking the narrative into organic, evenly-paced chapters along the story's natural beats — not wherever the original happened to break pages. Use it whenever there are no real chapters to parse.
options.source.nonNovel.example: e.g. turning a 5-part Reddit post or a back-and-forth email thread into a proper chaptered read.
options.language.targetLanguage.placehol: A translation instruction like 'translate Latin and Old English into Modern English', or a target language like 简体中文、English、日本語、한국어.
options.language.targetLanguage.label: Translation instruction or target language
options.language.translate.label: Translate
options.language.translate.tooltip: Translates fiction per the instruction or target language you type in once it's on. Most readers won't need this — leave it off if you already read the original.
options.language.translate.example: e.g. reading Russian fiction in English without losing the story.
options.language.nameLocalization.label: Localize names
options.language.nameLocalization.toolti: Reworks character and place names so they read naturally in the target language — fixes tongue-twisting transliterations and unreadable romanizations.
options.language.nameLocalization.exampl: e.g. taming a tangle of romanized pinyin names from Chinese or romaji names from Japansee into ones you can actually keep straight.
options.language.dialogueSubject.label: Restore dialogue subjects
options.language.dialogueSubject.tooltip: Japanese fictions often drop the subject and signal the speaker with verbal tics alone. This re-adds clear attribution so you always know who's talking.
options.language.dialogueSubject.example: e.g. turning a tic-laced line into '…,' she said, flicking her hair.
options.customInstruction.label: Anything else to tweak?
options.customInstruction.placeholder: Change it however you like — just tell me.
options.customInstruction.tooltip: Put any instruction you'd like to add that is not included in the options above. Make sure this doesn't conflict with the options above.
